package_info.why_malicious: All versions of the vm2 package prior to 3.9.11 are vulnerable to a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw (CVE-2022-36067) that allows attackers to escape the JavaScript sandbox and execute arbitrary shell commands on the host system. This undermines the core security guarantee of the package, making it dangerous to use in any context where untrusted code is executed.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when untrusted code is executed in the vm2 sandbox)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied code executed within the vm2 sandbox (via the run method or similar API)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Error.prepareStackTrace = function() { return process; }; throw new Error();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code customizes the Error.prepareStackTrace method to return the Node.js process object, then throws an error to trigger the stack trace mechanism, allowing access to the process object and enabling arbitrary command execution outside the sandbox.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code leverages a non-standard manipulation of the Error.prepareStackTrace method to break out of the intended sandbox isolation, exposing the process object which should be inaccessible to sandboxed code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, code running inside vm2 should not be able to access Node.js process or global objects, nor execute shell commands. This code bypasses those restrictions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Customizing Error.prepareStackTrace is sometimes used for debugging or custom error formatting, but never to intentionally expose process or global objects in a sandboxed environment.
key_indicators: Returning process or global objects from stack trace customization
Throwing errors to trigger stack trace manipulation

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after gaining access to process object via snippet_1)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied code executed within the vm2 sandbox

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after obtaining the process object, the code uses process.mainModule.require to import the child_process module and executes a shell command (e.g., 'id'), resulting in arbitrary command execution on the host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code executes shell commands from within a supposedly restricted sandbox, which is a clear violation of the sandbox's security model.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sandboxed code should never be able to execute arbitrary shell commands or access the child_process module.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of child_process occurs in trusted application code, not in sandboxed or untrusted code.
key_indicators: Loading child_process from within a sandbox
Executing shell commands from untrusted code

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits malicious code to be executed in the vm2 sandbox, overriding Error.prepareStackTrace to expose the process object.
attack_chain.leads_to: Access to Node.js process object from within the sandbox

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the exposed process object to require the child_process module and execute arbitrary shell commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the host system

behavioral_signatures: Overriding Error.prepareStackTrace in untrusted or sandboxed code
Access to process or global objects from within a sandbox
Use of process.mainModule.require to load sensitive modules (e.g., child_process) in sandboxed environments
Execution of shell commands from code running in a sandbox
file_indicators: References to process.mainModule.require or child_process in sandboxed code
network_indicators: Outbound connections initiated by child processes spawned from within a sandbox
Unexpected network activity from processes that should be isolated
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for any assignment to Error.prepareStackTrace in code executed within vm2 sandboxes, and flag any access to process, global, or use of process.mainModule.require. Audit for execution of shell commands or loading of sensitive modules (like child_process) from within sandboxed environments. Alert on any outbound network activity or filesystem access initiated by code that should be restricted to the sandbox.
